x: We have yet to win the team race in this classic race, and this year it seemed even less likely that we should do so, for we were without the assistance of Colin Collis, Eric Gebbett and Bob Plummer.
Colin Collis is weakening; having bashed the Club '7' and run quite well he only needs a few well directed words and perhaps he'll be changing in the stable at Windsor Castle again in 1958.

With Jack Brown in Cyprus and Colin Collis (temporarily we hope) retired it was to be expected that we would not retain our team title. Our chances were even further reduced when Eric Gebbett retired at nine miles after unwisely trying to stay with the leaders who were moving at a very hot pace.
If perseverance, courage and fortitude can produce a self-made athlete of top class, then Colin Collis, the subject of this article, is an admirable example.
Walker were well to the fore early on, and with Colin Collis, Archie Bedford, Len Bishop and Bob Plummer quite well placed, it seemed as if we might gain a team place in this well contested race.
Colin Collis, making a very successful comeback, was our first man home. He was closely followed by Eric Gebbett and Archie Bedford who both ran well in very difficult conditions.

Unfortunately, for a variety of reasons, Archie Bedford, John Davies, Colin Collis and Clive Shippen were unable to run, so with six to score and a "12 cup" in the offing we were able to start nine only.
Colin Collis really pulled one out of the bag to be our only runner under 24min. and earned his place in the Brighton team. It was grand to see Colin running so well.

…binson floundered along on the second and lost three places, his time of 26.18 being the fifteenth best of the day, and Colin Collis,who was entrusted with the vital stage from Mitcham to Purley after his brilliant run in the T.V.H. relay, had an almost complete breakdown and finished in a distresse…
Colin Collis, in a welcome return to form, produced the fastest time of our boys. The last effort of the winter season is the National Relay over the London to Brighton course.

With such a fast winning time many meritorious performances "down the field" are apt to be overlooked, but Colin Collis deserves special mention for his 11th place in 1h.50m.50s as does Bob Plummer for his best ever time of 1h.52m.54s.

After a final vote of thanks to Sid Roberts, voiced by Colin Collis, the meeting was adjourned. It is reported in some quarters, that Dave Martin Shepherd was in fact, last seen buying 'halves' all round.
From our mountain of mail the lucky (clever) winner who was correct except for one letter in one word was Colin Collis. Well done Colin, a dinner ticket is on it's way to you.

Surprises in the middle of the field were Chris Fairfield, John Hilton and our veteran ex marathon champion Colin Collis. Battling together for much of the race these three didn't realise they were fighting for two of the handicap prizes!
Colin Collis saved face for Belgrave to a certain extent with only one letter wrong in his entry and Bob Barnes was not far behind with just two letters incorrect.
There were seven correct solutions to the last crossword competition but the first one opened on May 1st was the entry from Colin Collis, always a staunch supporter of our competitions.

He was a shot putter and was introduced to us by his sportsmaster, Colin Collis. Colin very kindly sent us a photograph of the team and amongst those in it were Alan Black and his twin brother and one or two others who joined us for a while.

Colin Collis was third in the fourth Open run over the same distance and the team were placed second behind Victoria Park Harriers. In the London to Brighton relay we were 4th and six Club stage records were broken so keen was the pace set by the winners South London who were almost unbeatable at that time.
